capabilities.target: executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)
any recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox
executive's calendar (accept invite) and generated prep note draft

inputs.source: Inbound calendar invite with a free-text description, sendable by anyone including outside the company
The executive's own chat requests to the agent

instructions.note: The agent acts on any new invite automatically with no check on sender identity or invite content, then searches documents and emails attendees with no limit on which documents or which recipients are involved.

The instruction to 'find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees' lets the invite's attacker-editable free text effectively decide what gets read and who receives it, with no stated limit.

elements.name: Arbitrary/external invite sender and potential email recipient
Executive's drive (board materials, draft financial results)

controls.name: Verify calendar invite sender/domain before auto-accepting
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by checking the invite's authenticated sender/domain outside the model; does not depend on model capability.

controls.name: Treat invite description as untrusted data; strip or ignore embedded instructions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by parsing/sanitization outside the model, but sufficiently obfuscated instructions in free text may still evade a parser as attack sophistication grows.

controls.name: Bind outbound recipients to the calendar system of record, not free-text invite fields
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model by sourcing recipient addresses from the verified calendar record rather than attacker-editable invite fields; does not depend on model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate on external email sends, raw action review
controls.decay_rationale: A human-in-the-loop approval enforced in the orchestration layer before external sends, independent of model capability if review mode stays raw_action and volume stays low.

controls.name: Content-based DLP blocking restricted-sensitivity documents from external send
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model via classifier/pattern matching, but reformatting or summarization by a more capable model can evade content-based DLP.

controls.name: Independent, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions
controls.decay_rationale: A log written by the orchestration layer or a separate service, outside the model's control, remains accurate regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Rate limit on invites processed and briefs sent per period
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the orchestration layer as a hard count/time limit; does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): invite-controlled document search and unrestricted external email send

attack_path.note: Anyone can send the executive an invite with an attacker-controlled free-text description.
Agent auto-accepts the invite if the time is free and begins preparing, driven by the invite's content.
Agent searches and reads the executive's drive, including board materials and draft financial results, as 'related documents'.
Agent emails the brief, and any surfaced document content, to attendees; there is no recipient restriction or approval step, so a recipient can include the external inviter.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any new tool/integration added to this agent, or a model upgrade, without first adding sender verification and a mail recipient/content control keeps this at critical; watch the tool manifest and model version for changes.

evidence.observation: Agent accepts any new invite if the time is free and then finds related documents and emails a brief to attendees, with no check on sender identity or invite content.
Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite, and the invite description is free text written by the sender, creating an injectable instruction channel.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, which the agent's document search would surface as 'related documents'.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the brief and surfaced document content can be sent to attendees controlled by the inviter, including external parties.

recommendations.action: Verify the calendar invite sender/domain before auto-accepting, and treat the invite's free-text description as untrusted data that must never be interpreted as instructions to the agent.

Source outbound email recipients from the verified calendar system of record rather than the invite's editable fields, and require raw-action human approval before any brief is sent to a recipient outside the company domain.
Apply content-based data loss prevention to block restricted-sensitivity documents, such as board materials or draft financial results, from being summarized or attached into externally bound email.
Rate-limit the number of invites processed and briefs sent per time window to bound the blast radius of a flood of malicious invites.

findings.title: No independent audit trail of agent actions; oversight relies on a self-authored summary

forecast.watch_signal: A more capable model could write more persuasive but selectively incomplete daily summaries, or autonomy could expand further, without any independent record ever being added; watch for model version changes or expanded autonomy with no new, independently generated log.

evidence.observation: The daily summary is written by the agent itself, so there is no independent record of what the agent actually searched, read, or sent, which the same compromised agent could omit or misstate.
The agent acts on invites as they arrive and the executive only reviews a daily summary after the fact, relying entirely on the agent's own self-report for oversight.

recommendations.action: Generate the executive's daily summary from an independent, tamper-evident audit log produced by the orchestration layer, not by the agent itself, so a compromised agent cannot hide or misstate its own actions.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe how drive.search_and_read, mail.send, or calendar.accept_and_prepare authenticate the agent itself when invoking these tools.
This inbound flow carries the invite into the agent; it does not itself carry organizational data outward, so disclosure risk is realized on the outbound mail flow instead.
Volume risk from unbounded invite processing is already assessed on the upstream invite flow; this flow does not add a separate availability concern.
The only declared capability against this store, drive.search_and_read, is read-only; the design grants the agent no write path to this store.
No declared capability performs bulk deletion or resource exhaustion against this read-only document store.
The daily summary is reviewed internally by the executive and is not described as being sent or exposed outside the organization.
No capability depends on this store's availability to perform calendar, drive, or mail actions; its loss would not block agent operation.
This external party is outside the agent's trust domain; the design does not claim to establish non-repudiation for actions taken by outside senders, only for the agent's own actions.

rating.rationale: The design lets anyone reach the executive's calendar, which drives an unattended pipeline (accept, then search the drive, then email attendees) with no sender verification, no recipient restriction, no approval step, and no independent audit trail. The lethal-trifecta path (untrusted invite, confidential/restricted drive read, unrestricted external send) is rated critical at both inherent and residual because no declared control narrows or severs it; the missing independent-audit-trail property is rated high. Forecast equals residual because both findings are already at their ceiling; the single highest-leverage fix is binding mail recipients to the calendar system of record plus a raw-action approval gate on external sends.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; actual tool wiring, authentication, and guardrails were not independently verified.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided, so capability scope (for example, the exact drive_read query scope and calendar.accept_and_prepare internals) is inferred from narrative runtime notes; confidence on exact mechanics is medium.

No approval, DLP, or logging configuration was supplied beyond the explicit statement that mail.send has no recipient restriction and no approval step; the complete absence of controls is taken as given, but undocumented controls, if any exist, could lower residual risk.
